note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one City of Orem park page, the page that gives the park its Location line, its amenity list and, at two of the three, its reservation rule, plus the City's parks guide, which names the park, and the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Twelve pickleball courts, the largest set in Orem, split by the City into two sixes with different rules.

The amenity line is "12 Pickleball Courts (6 Courts reservable, 6 Courts open for public use)", and the page says it again lower down: "6 Pickleball courts can be reserved for private use" through the City's reservation link, and "6 of the other courts are for public use and will be held to the standard of using the 'Paddle Rotation System.'"

Around the courts the City lists three playgrounds, a splash pad open seasonally from Memorial Day to Labor Day, a rentable big pavilion with a capacity of 75, a nature leisure walk, and hammock and slack-line timber poles. Anyone "interested in hosting a tournament or an event specifically geared toward pickleball" is asked to call (801) 229-7154.
slots.getting_there:
650 E 1400 S, Orem, UT 84097, in the south-east of the city. The City writes the address as a Utah grid line, 650 East on 1400 South, with no city, state or postcode. The US Census address geocoder matched it as written, at house-number level, in the incorporated place Orem city, Utah County; the postcode is the geocoder's.

The City publishes nothing about parking. Its amenity list does not mention restrooms either, and since the Sharon and Bonneville lists do, that absence is recorded as unknown rather than as a no.
slots.what_to_expect:
Twelve courts is enough for a rotation, and the City has written one down: arrive with a paddle for each player and put them on the next open rack. Six of the twelve can be booked for private use, so on any visit some of them may be spoken for.

The page carries one hours line, "Hours of Operations: Monday-Saturday from 10:00am-8:00pm", and it belongs to the splash pad, under the heading "Splash Pad Hours". Nothing ties it to the courts, so court hours here are not stated.

The City states no price, no lighting, no surface and no indoor or outdoor answer for these courts.

faqs.q: What is the Paddle Rotation System?
faqs.a: The City's queue for the six public courts: waiting players put a paddle for each player on the next open rack, and when a game ends the players announce "Open Court" and the court goes to the paddles on the rack.
Not stated. No price appears on the page and the word free does not either.

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts in a 5.2-acre park in north-east Orem, reserved for one purpose only.

The description reads "The park has a large playground and six pickleball courts." The amenity line reads "6 Pickleball Courts" and then, in a bracket, the whole reservation policy: "(we currently ONLY reserve pickleball courts for the city's tournaments, not for any other private use)." So on any day the City is not running a tournament the six courts are walk-on, and on a tournament day they are the City's.

The park is a seasonal one in the City's telling: "In the winter, Sharon Park is often used for tubing and sledding. In the summer, it's a nice shady retreat for families." The amenity list also has a playground, restrooms, a 0.42-mile walking path and a large pavilion with barbecue braziers that seats 120.
slots.getting_there:
600 N 300 E, Orem, UT 84057, in the north-east of the city. The City's Location line is a Utah grid address, 600 North on 300 East, and the US Census address geocoder matched it as written in the incorporated place Orem city, Utah County, with the postcode 84057.

The imported dataset had this park one block off, at 500 N 300 E, and a second imported row placed it at 285 500 N; the City's line replaces both. The City publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are in the amenity list.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six walk-on courts, unless the City is running a tournament. There is no booking link to check and no private block to work around, but there is no tournament calendar on the page either, so the one thing that can take the courts is the one thing the page does not date.

Six courts is three games at once, and the City states no queue rule here of the kind it posts at Hillcrest. It states no price, no hours, no lighting and no surface, and the page says nothing about whether the courts are indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: No. The City writes that it currently reserves these courts "ONLY" for its own tournaments, "not for any other private use".
Not stated. No price appears on the page and the word free does not either; the reservation rule says who may book, not what it costs.

slots.description:
Four lighted pickleball courts in a 5.2-acre park, the one Orem venue where the City states lighting.

The amenity line is "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts", and the description says it again from the other direction: "enjoy a game of Pickleball on one of the four new Pickleball courts". "Lighted" is the City's word, and it is the word needed before a court is marked as lit here. "New" is also the City's word, undated, and it is printed as written.

The courts sit in a park the City describes as offering "wide open spaces and a number of amenities": one large pavilion that "Will seat 100", one small pavilion for sixteen, four barbecue braziers, a full-size basketball court, a tennis court listed separately from the four pickleball courts, a shade-covered playground, a walking path and restrooms.
slots.getting_there:
1450 N 800 W, Orem, UT 84057. The City writes the address as a Utah grid line, 1450 North on 800 West, and the US Census address geocoder matched it as written in the incorporated place Orem city, Utah County, with the postcode 84057.

The City's own description opens "Located on the Northeast corner of Orem", while its Location line reads 800 West; what publishes here is the address, not the compass point. The City publishes nothing about parking. Restrooms are in the amenity list.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts with lights, which in Orem is the difference between a venue where play after dark is a published fact and two where it is a guess. The City says nothing about how late the lights run or when the park closes, so the lighting is a capability rather than a timetable.

There is no reservation rule here. The page invites visitors to "enjoy a game of Pickleball" and says nothing about booking, which is the thinnest basis of the three Orem parks for calling the courts open play.

Four courts is two games at once. The City states no price, no surface, no hours and no indoor or outdoor answer.

faqs.a: Yes. The City's amenity line is "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts"; it states no closing time, so how late the lights run is not published.
Not stated. No price appears on the page and the word free does not either.
